children: India's infrastructure output (ININFR=ECI) grew 4.8% year-on-year in August as strong cement and electricity output outweighed weakness in energy-related sectors, according to government data released on Monday.
This is the third data release under the new series, which uses 2022-23 as the base year and expands the core sector basket to include iron ore.
Infrastructure output had grown a revised 5% in July from a year earlier, the data showed.
• Cement output rose 12.5% in August from a revised 12.7% increase in July.
• Steel production increased 3.4% last month, compared with a revised 1.9% growth in July.
• Electricity generation rose 11.6% in August, as compared with a revised 8.4% increase in July.
• Iron ore production rose 5.5% in August, compared with a rise of 29.5% in July.
• Refinery products output rose 2.6% in August versus a revised 3% rise a month earlier.
• Coal production fell 3.8% in August, compared with a rise of 7.6% the prior month.
• Crude oil output fell 3.6% in August, compared with a fall of 5.3% in July.
• Fertilizer production declined 12.4% in August, following an 8% contraction in the prior month.
• Natural gas production shrank 4.9% in August, as compared with a revised drop of 3% in July.
• The cumulative infrastructure output growth for April-August increased year-on-year to 4.3% from 2.4% in the corresponding period last year
